description: REVTeX 4.2 for APS journals, two-column reprint format, with footnotes at the foot of the page (nofootinbib; b22, owner item RX-FN). Under aps the class sets footinbib (aps4-2.rtx l.649): every \footnote body is written to the notes .bib with \immediate\write and printed inside the bibliography (revtex4-2.cls l.7245-7300), where General's footnotes with block children broke: 'Use of \ltx@xfootnote doesn't match its definition', 'Unbalanced write command', 'Missing \endcsname inserted' (38 cells at TeX's 100-error stop), 'Something's wrong--perhaps a missing \item' or \unskip at \BibitemShut in main.bbl, and 135 more branches failed the footnote check: 1,573 failing not-denied revtex4-2-aps.A branches in GitHub run 41584963423. A bibliography made only of footnotes also left revtex's own \label{LastBibItem} undefined on a settled build in 3 documents (39 branches). REVTeX_APS.md l.155 allows either option ('Body-footnote position is controlled by footinbib/nofootinbib and journal defaults'); the class reads nofootinbib after aps4-2.rtx (\@options, l.7675, after \@process@society, l.7670), and aps's bracketed citations do not force endnotes back (aps4-2.rtx l.664-675). With footnotes at the foot General's footnotes reach the class's footnote code, so the preamble redefines its \make@footnotetext (l.508-522), copied from revtex4-2.cls (4.2f) with the change aastex.json makes to the same code: the \vadjust{\vskip\z@skip} after the footnote's last line is added only in horizontal mode, since footnotehyper (General's footnotes) releases its saved notes through the class's \@footnotetext after \unvbox, in internal vertical mode. aps4-2.rtx's \@makefntext (l.438) already takes paragraphs (\long); the class's \@mpmakefntext, which aastex.json also makes \long, is never used by revtex4-2, so it is left alone. A footnote that ends in horizontal mode with no paragraph break sets as before. The class's preamble builder also relaxes \@endpbox, \do@row@strut and \ar@align@mcell (b22, owner item R2), as array's own \@mkpream does (array.sty 2026/02/24 v2.7b l.432-434) and as aastex.json does for the same code: when a way's package brings array (box.awesomebox: awesomebox.sty l.61), revtex4-2 swaps in its own copies of array's internals at \begin{document} (\switch@array, l.1038-1110), whose \@mkpream@array@new (l.1604) calls \@mkpream@relax (l.1569-1576, 1658-1666), which relaxes \@startpbox but not \@endpbox; array's \xdef then expanded \@endpbox and its \color@endgroup's \ifvmode, so a p-column table begun in vertical mode stopped at 'Extra \or' (d7db59cac9bd98fa335b7, a tbl.tabular@grid table at l.197) or hung with no log (19 of the 20 revtex4-2-aps.A no-log documents of the run, 728 branches, hold awesomebox and a p-column table). awesomebox stays fit (363 not-denied branches, 175 passing). Without array the class keeps its own \switch@tabular code, whose preamble builder never calls \@mkpream@relax (only longtable's \LT@array@new does, l.5212, and tbl.longtable is not fit under revtex4-2), so the line changes nothing there. A third line (b22, owner item revtex O1, an interim until Flouest's contents provide the name themselves) gives article's \contentsname, \listfigurename and \listtablename, which revtex4-2 never defines (it names its titles \tocname, \lofname and \lotname, revtex4-2.cls l.7493-7495), and makes revtex's titles print them: General's contents rename \contentsname ('Command \contentsname undefined', 9 branches of GitHub run 41584963423), and tocloft, which General's contents looks load, sets its titles from them ('\cfttoctitlename ->\contentsname' undefined at a library contents way's \tableofcontents, 3). The titles print as before unless renamed; toc.tocloft's own \providecommand lines then find the names given.
